title: Windsor Castle: King Charles's 'most haunted' royal residence with over 25 ghost sightings
excerpt: King Charles III has a number of royal residences to move between, but one of his favorites is reportedly Windsor Castle, said to be the 'most haunted.'
content:
Rebecca Russell, Jasmine Carey, Julianna Salinas

Sat, October 31, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC

As Britain's sovereign, King Charles possesses numerous royal properties across the country.

From Buckingham Palace to Balmoral Castle, and including the Palace of Holyroodhouse, accommodation options are plentiful. Nevertheless, one of his preferred properties seems to be Windsor Castle. While this historic residence attracts many members of the Royal Family, it apparently harbors a supernatural dimension.

This reputation stems from reports identifying it as the "most haunted" among King Charles's residences. The designation comes from more than 25 documented ghost sightings over the years, enough to unsettle even the bravest visitor.

The castle's construction commenced in 1070, and it has served numerous monarchs throughout history, beginning with Henry I. Evidently, certain monarchs developed such strong attachments to the property that their presence allegedly persists beyond death.

Notable monarchs reportedly maintaining a spectral presence within the castle include Henry VIII, Queen Elizabeth I, and King George III. According to Visit Britain, Queen Elizabeth I's footsteps can be heard on the bare floorboards around the castle, reports the Express.

She has also been sighted, with Queen Elizabeth II once claiming that she and Princess Margaret witnessed paranormal activity in the castle together, which they believed to be Elizabeth I.

Another spirit said to inhabit the beloved castle's corridors is King George III. Accounts indicate he roams the chamber beneath the library, where he devoted considerable time during his final years while experiencing mental health challenges.

Witnesses are believed to have observed a figure resembling him "looking longingly out of the window." Additional sightings place him in a bedroom within the castle, with one officer reportedly claiming to have encountered the former monarch mere days following his death.

According to the officer's account, guards were conducting their regular duties past the King's window when the commanding officer observed the unmistakable figure of the King positioned in his customary spot observing the parade.

The officer issued the command, "Eyes right," and as they turned, they witnessed the figure bearing a resemblance to the late King salute.

If this isn't unsettling enough, historical records spanning many years also indicate that King Henry VIII can be heard within the castle.

It is believed that they hear the hobbling sound, which he used to make when he walked around the castle, as he was so obese and found it hard to walk.

While these accounts are frightening, particularly during Halloween, they seemingly do not discourage the royals from regularly utilizing the castle.

King Charles performs much of his royal work at the royal residence, including hosting state visits. Prince William and Princess Catherine, whose own home is just a short drive from the castle, also spend a lot of their time working from the residence.
